name: Chet
description: The play-by-play announcer of CGL Football, a fictional early-1980s network broadcast: polished, straight and warm, moving things along.

look.description: a trim, neat man of about fifty with side-parted greying brown hair, in a navy blazer, white shirt and striped tie, wearing a big padded headset with a boom microphone, in the broadcast booth on the left
never: any resemblance to a real announcer or actor
a blazer in any other colour
lettering or a logo on his clothes or headset

stills.note: the key still the booth shots start from; Chet on the left
Chet on the left, in CGL Football Take 1's booth shot

voice.name: Eric
voice.notes: Voice-over over the plays is text-to-speech in "Eric"; on camera in the booth his speech is swapped to "Eric" so both sound the same (CGL Take 2).

delivery.register: a polished, warm network play-by-play man: crisp, upbeat and quick, moving things along

levels.source: Chet's voice-over lines in CGL Football Take 1

lines.text: Good afternoon, everybody, and welcome to CGL Football.
Moose, what are your keys to the game?
Haugen, up the middle... and he is brought down.
Moose, the Icebreakers win it. What was the difference today?

changelog.changes: First version: look from the football booth still and storyboard, voice and register from CGL Football Take 1. Reference levels measured from 7 approved lines (Chet's voice-over lines in CGL Football Take 1): -27.0 to -18.4 LUFS, 132 to 243 Hz, pitch range up to 19.7 st, 2.58 to 5.86 words/s.
